name: Cochamó valley to La Junta
why: An old ox-cart trail through rainforest into a valley of granite walls and waterfalls, often called the Yosemite of Chile.
book: A camping reservation at La Junta is compulsory (cochamo.com); register at the Visitor Center by the trailhead. Access to the trail closes at 15:00 (14:00 in March and April). Cochamó is 2.5 h by road from Puerto Montt; the last 10 km of gravel to the trailhead need a 4x4.
water: Streams and the river all the way; treat it.
dangers: Deep mud for long stretches, all summer.
Paso de la Muerte: a narrow, exposed bit above the Cochamó river.
After heavy rain the Río Piedra plank crossing may be impassable for a day or more.
Pack horses have right of way: step a metre off the trail.
turnaround: Not past the Descansadero by 13:00: go back and sleep near the trailhead.

points.name: Cochamó trailhead and Visitor Center
points.note: At the end of the road above Cochamó: register at the Visitor Center and show your camping reservation.

points.name: Río Piedra crossing
points.note: About an hour in. The bridge was washed away in 2023; the crossing on planks can be cut by high water.

points.name: Descansadero
points.note: The rest stop 2-3 hours in, after most of the climbing. Mud and rock slabs follow.

points.name: La Junta
points.note: Meadows where the Río La Junta meets the Cochamó, under granite walls. Camp at the reserved site; return the same way.
